headline: Over 200 attackers raze Mirpur health center using heavy machinery
summary: The Radda MCH-FP center was demolished and looted, destroying critical government vaccines and medical equipment worth 1.5 crore BDT.
details: Over 200 masked attackers armed with local weapons stormed the Radda MCH-FP healthcare center in Mirpur around midnight last Thursday. The attackers took security guards hostage, tied their hands and feet, and looted medical equipment, medicines, and government vaccines.

Using heavy machinery, the group demolished one permanent and three semi-permanent buildings within the facility. The executive director of the center, Nasrin Akhtar, reported losses exceeding 1 crore BDT, including the destruction of ultrasound machines and generators.
The Democratic Rights Committee has condemned the attack, calling it a 'terrorist attack' on the public health system and the right to live, especially during ongoing measles and dengue epidemics.
Allegations have surfaced that the attack was carried out under the banner of the 'Sommona Dokandar Somobay Somiti Limited' and was a planned land-grabbing attempt backed by political influence.

Four people have been arrested and sent to jail in connection with the case filed at Shah Ali Police Station. The DMP commissioner has ordered a probe into whether police negligence allowed the demolition to happen overnight.

The Democratic Rights Committee is demanding the immediate arrest of the main planners, the recovery of the 10-katha plot of land, and the reconstruction of the clinic to restore essential health services for poor mothers and children.

headline_marked: Home Minister: [[Awami League will not be allowed to do politics]] in Bangladesh
headline: Home Minister: Awami League will not be allowed to do politics in Bangladesh
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed says those involved in genocide and crimes against humanity over the last 17 years will find no place in the country's politics.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed declared that the 'fascist' Awami League will never be allowed to engage in politics on Bangladeshi soil again, following the mass uprising.

Speaking at a rally in Dhaka's Dholaikhal, he stated that everyone involved in genocide and crimes against humanity will face trial through the International Crimes Tribunal, with more tribunals potentially being added.

Addressing Sheikh Hasina's reported plans to return in December, the Minister described her as a convicted criminal and stated that the government has formally requested her return via the India-Bangladesh extradition treaty.
He urged the government of the country where convicted criminals are staying to return them, emphasizing that they will face international-standard trials and have the right to appeal.
Salahuddin Ahmed also called for a fundamental change in political culture, urging party members to move away from person-centric slogans and focus on the fight against fascism.
The Minister criticized opposition groups for calling for a 'one-point' demand and long marches just seven months into the current government's term, calling such moves baseless.
Regarding fuel price hikes, he explained that the increase was necessary to prevent smuggling and align with international market prices, promising that prices will decrease as global rates drop.
He concluded by calling for national unity to consolidate the democratic process and protect the gains of the blood-stained mass uprising.

He urged the government of the country where convicted criminals are staying to return them, emphasizing that they will face international-standard trials and have the right to appeal.
